learnings: A descriptor is any class attribute with `__get__`; adding `__set__`/`__delete__` makes it a data descriptor.
Lookup order: data descriptors → instance `__dict__` → non-data descriptors → class attributes.
`__set_name__` tells a descriptor which attribute name it was assigned to, so one class serves many fields.
pitfalls: A cached non-data descriptor is shadowed by the instance dict after the first access – that is the trick, not a bug.
